answer: Persistent Behavioural Fingerprint Scoring. Each identity's action history is compressed into a lightweight state vector stored at a shared registry inlet; agents earn trust only when their current-epoch vector stays within a bounded distance of prior epochs. Drift beyond threshold freezes privileges until re-verified. An attacker must sustain coherent behaviour across many epochs per fake identity, multiplying operational cost linearly with fleet size—each pearl of consistent history must be built separately. Honest agents coast; synthetic fleets drown in the ocean of upkeep.
